experiences.name: Diavolezza Glacier Skiing
experiences.description: Experience world-class skiing on the Diavolezza glacier near Pontresina, offering stunning runs with panoramic views of Piz Palü and Bernina peaks. Suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers with over 10km of marked pistes and off-piste opportunities.

experiences.name: Bernina Express Scenic Winter Rail Journey
experiences.description: Board the iconic UNESCO-listed Bernina Express from Poschiavo station, winding through dramatic Alpine landscapes, frozen lakes, and snow-covered viaducts. The route passes the famous Brusio spiral viaduct just minutes from Poschiavo, offering breathtaking winter scenery.
experiences.location: Poschiavo Railway Station, Via Principale, Poschiavo

experiences.name: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails
experiences.description: Explore serene cross-country ski trails departing from Alp Grüm, a high-altitude stop above Poschiavo accessible by the Bernina railway. Glide through pristine snow with sweeping views of the Palü glacier and the Poschiavo valley below.

experiences.name: Snowshoeing in Val da Camp
experiences.description: Strap on snowshoes and trek through the enchanting Val da Camp side valley near Poschiavo, a quiet and pristine winter wilderness. Guided tours reveal local Alpine flora, frozen waterfalls, and traditional Graubünden stone farmhouses buried in snow.

experiences.name: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with an authentic Graubünden dinner in Poschiavo's historic village center. Savor local cheese fondue, hearty Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with alpine cheese and vegetables), and Valtellina wines in a cozy centuries-old stone restaurant.
experiences.location: Historic Village Center, Via Principale, Poschiavo

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and travel day.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 22:30. Take the train toward Chur and then connect toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express or regional rail. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama upon late arrival. Unpack and settle in.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: Meal on the plane or grab a quick bite at Zurich Airport (budget CHF 10–15 at airport kiosks or Migros/Coop food counters).
meals.dinner: Pick up a sandwich, snack, or ready meal at a Coop or Migros convenience store at the train station before boarding (budget CHF 8–12). Eat on the train.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina line can be scenic even at night. Confirm train schedules in advance as late-night connections to Poschiavo may be limited — consider booking a taxi from Tirano or St. Moritz if trains have stopped running. Keep CHF cash handy for taxis. Rest well for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely start, enjoy the included B&B breakfast and take a short orientation walk around Poschiavo village. Explore the charming historic center, the Piazza Comunale, and the Spanish Quarter — a unique architectural gem built by locals who worked in Spain. Get your bearings and pick up any supplies at the local Coop supermarket.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Poschiavo valley slopes or inquire at the B&B about beginner-friendly ski rental options nearby. Visit the local tourist office to get maps of the Alp Grüm cross-country trails and plan the week. If feeling energetic, take the Bernina Express train up to Alp Grüm station (a short scenic ride) to scout the cross-country ski trail network and enjoy panoramic views of the Palü Glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo village. Stroll along the lakeside of Lago di Poschiavo as the sun sets over the mountains. Relax at the B&B and plan the rest of the week.

meals.breakfast: Included B&B breakfast — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Self-catered picnic from Coop supermarket in Poschiavo — grab bread, local cheese, salami, and fruit (budget CHF 8–10).
meals.dinner: Dine at Ristorante Croce Federale or a local trattoria in Poschiavo. Order a simple pasta or risotto dish (budget CHF 18–25). Alternatively, cook a simple meal if the B&B has kitchen access.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express train between Poschiavo and Alp Grüm is included in the Swiss Travel Pass if you have one — otherwise a short regional ticket costs approximately CHF 8–12 each way. Buy a regional day pass if planning multiple train rides.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of cross-country skiing on Alp Grüm Trails. Take the Rhaetian Railway (Bernina line) from Poschiavo up to Alp Grüm station (approx. 20–30 min). Rent cross-country skis at or near the station if not already rented. Begin exploring the serene groomed cross-country trails departing from Alp Grüm at 2,091m altitude. The trails offer stunning views of the Palü Glacier and surrounding peaks. Start with the easier beginner loops to warm up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the intermediate Alp Grüm trail network. Pack a thermos of hot tea or coffee and a packed lunch to enjoy on the mountain. Take breaks to photograph the dramatic alpine scenery. Try the longer trail loops that wind through snow-covered forests and open alpine meadows.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Warm up at the B&B with a hot shower. Head into the village for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included B&B breakfast.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared the night before or bought at Coop — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and a thermos of hot drink (budget CHF 6–8). Eating on the mountain saves significant money vs. mountain restaurants.
meals.dinner: Try Osteria Salis or a local pizzeria in Poschiavo for a hearty pizza or pasta (budget CHF 15–22). Pair with a local Valposchiavo wine for a treat.

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski rental at Alp Grüm or nearby costs approximately CHF 20–35/day. Dress in warm layers — Alp Grüm sits above 2,000m and temperatures can be well below freezing. Sunscreen is essential even in winter at altitude. Check trail conditions at the tourist office the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Diavolezza ski area near Pontresina/St. Moritz (accessible via Bernina Express train from Poschiavo — approx. 1 hour). Diavolezza offers spectacular downhill skiing with views of the Morteratsch Glacier and Piz Palü. Purchase a half-day ski pass to keep costs down (approx. CHF 40–55 for a half-day adult pass). Rent ski equipment at the base if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza. Try the famous Diavolezza glacier run — a long, scenic descent toward Morteratsch. Beginners can stick to the easier blue runs near the top station. Take the cable car up for panoramic views even if skiing ability is limited.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Rest tired legs at the B&B. Optional: soak feet in warm water and do light stretching.

meals.breakfast: Included B&B breakfast — eat well before a big ski day.
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch again to avoid expensive mountain restaurant prices (CHF 6–8 self-catered vs. CHF 25–40 at mountain restaurants). Find a sunny spot on the mountain to eat.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple budget meal at the B&B if kitchen access is available — pasta with jarred sauce from Coop (CHF 5–8 total). Or grab a takeaway pizza slice from a local bakery in Poschiavo (CHF 4–6).

day_by_day.notes: Train from Poschiavo to Ospizio Bernina/Pontresina costs approx. CHF 15–20 each way without a pass. A Swiss Travel Pass covers this route and saves money if you plan multiple train trips. Diavolezza ski pass is a splurge but worth it for the glacier experience. Book train tickets in advance via the SBB app.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Alp Grüm for a second day of cross-country skiing. Now more familiar with the trails, push further and tackle the longer, more challenging routes. The trail toward Cavaglia offers a beautiful descent through the valley with views of the Bernina massif. Enjoy the peaceful, crowd-free atmosphere compared to the larger ski resorts.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skiing, stop at the historic Alp Grüm restaurant/refuge for a warming cup of soup or hot chocolate as a small treat (budget CHF 5–8). Then take the train back down toward Poschiavo and stop at Cavaglia mid-station to explore the famous 'Giants' Cauldrons' (Marmitte dei Giganti) — glacial potholes carved into rock, visible even in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo. Visit the local Coop to stock up on supplies. Spend a relaxed evening at the B&B reviewing photos and planning the final days.

meals.breakfast: Included B&B breakfast.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the mountain (CHF 6–8 self-catered).
meals.dinner: Cook at the B&B or try a local Valposchiavo specialty — Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables) at a local restaurant. This regional dish is hearty and affordable (CHF 16–22).

day_by_day.notes: Cavaglia stop is a short detour on the Bernina line — check train schedules to ensure you can stop and catch the next train down to Poschiavo without a long wait. The Giants' Cauldrons are a free natural attraction. Wear waterproof boots as the area can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Winter snowshoeing day — rent snowshoes in Poschiavo (approx. CHF 15–20/day) and explore the trails around Lago di Poschiavo and the lower valley. The lake often partially freezes in February, creating a magical winter landscape. Follow marked snowshoe trails through the forest above the village for great views of the valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Bernina Express train north to St. Moritz for an afternoon of window shopping, people-watching, and exploring the famous resort town on a budget. Walk around the frozen Lake St. Moritz (free), visit the Engadine Museum (small entry fee ~CHF 10), or simply enjoy the glamorous alpine atmosphere without spending much. Browse the village and grab a coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate the last full active day of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Included B&B breakfast.
meals.lunch: In St. Moritz, find the Coop or Migros supermarket for a budget lunch (CHF 8–12). Avoid the expensive resort restaurants. Alternatively, pack lunch from Poschiavo.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a farewell dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant. Try the Ristorante Albrici or similar — a two-course meal with local wine (budget CHF 28–38). This is the trip's one planned splurge dinner.

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the world's most expensive ski resorts but is free to walk around and enjoy. Avoid buying anything in the luxury shops! The train ride from Poschiavo to St. Moritz on the Bernina line is itself a UNESCO World Heritage experience — sit by the window and enjoy the views. Saturday may be busier on the trains — book seats in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Poschiavo. Enjoy a leisurely last B&B breakfast. Take a slow morning walk around the village one final time — visit the Reformed Church and the Catholic Church of San Vittore, both historic landmarks. Browse the Sunday atmosphere of the village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up and check out of the B&B. Depending on your departure flight or onward travel, take the Bernina Express toward Chur or Tirano (Italy side) for your connection. If time allows before departure, stop at Ospizio Bernina (the highest point of the Bernina line at 2,253m) for a final look at the stunning alpine landscape and the Lago Bianco reservoir.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Zurich or your departure airport via train connections through Chur. Allow ample time for connections — Swiss trains are punctual but the Bernina line journey takes time. Depart Switzerland with incredible alpine memories.

meals.breakfast: Included final B&B breakfast — eat well before the journey.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and a sandwich from Coop for the train journey (CHF 6–10). Eat on the scenic Bernina Express.
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Zurich Airport — Coop or Migros at the airport offer affordable options (CHF 10–15). Or dine at a mid-range airport restaurant if time and budget allow.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at the B&B — confirm with hosts the evening before. The Bernina Express to Chur takes approximately 2.5 hours; from Chur to Zurich is another 1.5 hours by fast train. Total journey to Zurich Airport is approximately 4–5 hours from Poschiavo — plan accordingly based on your flight time. Validate all train tickets before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Travel day. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit from airport to Poschiavo. Take the train from Zurich or transfer via St. Moritz/Tirano toward Poschiavo. Enjoy the night views of the Swiss countryside en route.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Check in, unpack, and settle in. Grab a light snack if the B&B has anything available, or pick up something at a convenience store near the station before the final leg of the journey.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Airport or in-transit meal – budget CHF 15–25 at a train station café or airport restaurant
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack from a convenience store or vending machine near Poschiavo station (CHF 5–10). Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at 22:30. Factor in customs, baggage claim, and a 2–3 hour transfer to Poschiavo via train (Zurich HB → Chur → St. Moritz → Poschiavo on the Bernina line, or a taxi/shuttle from a closer hub). Pre-book a taxi if arriving after last train connections. Get a good night's sleep – big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Slow, relaxed start after the late arrival. Enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast and take a short orientation walk through Poschiavo's charming historic village center. Explore the Piazza Comunale and the Italian-influenced architecture unique to this southern Graubünden valley. Pick up a local trail map and get your ski/snowshoe gear sorted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snowshoeing in Val da Camp – Strap on snowshoes and trek through the enchanting Val da Camp side valley near Poschiavo. This quiet, forested valley is perfect for easing into the alpine environment after travel. The trail is accessible and scenic, offering stunning views of snow-draped peaks and frozen streams. Duration: approximately 2–3 hours at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo village for a warm, authentic dinner. Enjoy the Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner experience in the historic village – the perfect way to warm up and celebrate the start of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast included – enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and hot drinks
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light bite at a local bakery/café in Poschiavo village (CHF 12–18) – try a local pastry or panino
meals.dinner: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner at a local restaurant in Poschiavo (CHF 30–45 per person including a glass of local wine)

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today – your body needs to adjust after the late arrival and travel fatigue. Val da Camp snowshoeing requires no special skill level and is a wonderful gentle introduction to the area. Rent snowshoes in Poschiavo if you don't have your own (approx. CHF 15–20/day).

day_by_day.morning: Diavolezza Glacier Skiing – Head to Diavolezza near Pontresina for a world-class skiing experience on the glacier. Take the early train from Poschiavo toward Pontresina (via the Bernina line) and then the Diavolezza cable car up to 2,978m. Morning sessions offer the best snow conditions and fewer crowds. Enjoy sweeping runs with panoramic views of Piz Palü and the Morteratsch Glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza through the afternoon. Try the famous Diavolezza-Morteratsch glacier run (approximately 10km), one of the most spectacular descents in the Alps. Take a break at the Diavolezza mountain restaurant for lunch with incredible views. Head back down by mid-afternoon to catch the return train to Poschiavo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Rest and freshen up at the B&B. Head into the village for a relaxed dinner at a local trattoria or pizzeria.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast – fuel up well before a full ski day
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant at Diavolezza – self-service or table service (CHF 20–35 per person). Try the Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) to warm up
meals.dinner: Local trattoria in Poschiavo – pasta, risotto, or local meat dishes (CHF 25–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ski pass for Diavolezza costs approximately CHF 60–75 per day. Ski rental in Pontresina or at the base is available (CHF 40–55/day for skis, boots, and poles). The Bernina Express train from Poschiavo to Pontresina takes about 45–60 minutes – check the RhB timetable and book in advance. Dress in warm layers; glacier altitude means temperatures can be significantly colder than the valley.

day_by_day.morning: Bernina Express Scenic Winter Rail Journey – Board the iconic UNESCO-listed Bernina Express from Poschiavo station. Wind through dramatic alpine scenery including the famous Brusio spiral viaduct, snow-covered Alp Grüm, the Bernina Pass, and down into the Engadin valley toward St. Moritz. This is one of the most spectacular train journeys in the world, especially in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in St. Moritz or Pontresina and spend the afternoon exploring. Visit the St. Moritz village, browse the upscale shops (window shopping is free!), or rent skis and enjoy a few runs on the Corviglia ski area above St. Moritz for a taste of the famous resort. Alternatively, take a leisurely walk along the frozen Lake St. Moritz.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo on the Bernina line in the early evening, watching the sunset alpenglow on the peaks. Dinner at the B&B if offered, or at a cozy local restaurant in Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before boarding the train
meals.lunch: Lunch in St. Moritz – try a mid-range restaurant or a mountain hut near Corviglia (CHF 25–40). Avoid the ultra-luxury spots to stay on budget
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner in Poschiavo – local Valposchiavo cuisine such as polenta with braised meat or local cheese dishes (CHF 25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express panoramic rail ticket from Poschiavo to St. Moritz costs approximately CHF 30–50 depending on class and reservation. Book panoramic car seats in advance through RhB (Rhaetian Railway) for the best views. The round trip can be done in a day comfortably. If you choose to ski at Corviglia, a half-day ski pass is available (approx. CHF 45–55).

day_by_day.morning: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails – Take the Bernina train up to Alp Grüm station (2,091m), a stunning high-altitude stop perched above Poschiavo with sweeping views of the Palü glacier. Strap on cross-country skis and explore the serene groomed trails through pristine alpine scenery. The trails here are peaceful and far less crowded than the downhill resorts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cross-country skiing or switch to a snowshoe exploration around the Alp Grüm area. The views of the Valposchiavo below and the surrounding glaciated peaks are extraordinary. Take time to simply sit, breathe the mountain air, and absorb the silence of the high Alps. Head back down to Poschiavo by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening in Poschiavo. Visit the local Museo di Poschiavo to learn about the valley's unique cultural heritage (Italian-speaking Swiss enclave). Enjoy a relaxed dinner and perhaps a glass of local Graubünden wine or a hot Bombardino (egg-cream ski drink) at a village bar.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the B&B or a snack at the Alp Grüm restaurant/café (CHF 10–20) – the restaurant there has basic hot food and drinks with an incredible view
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Poschiavo – try Ristorante Croce Federale or similar local establishment (CHF 28–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski rental is available in Poschiavo or Pontresina (CHF 20–30/day). The Alp Grüm trails are generally well-maintained but check conditions with the local tourist office. Train from Poschiavo to Alp Grüm takes about 20 minutes and costs a few CHF – consider a regional day pass for unlimited train travel on the Bernina line (approx. CHF 30–40).

day_by_day.morning: Return to Diavolezza for a second skiing day – now that you know the mountain, make the most of it. Focus on runs you didn't get to try on Day 3, or perfect your technique on favorite slopes. The glacier run in morning light is particularly magical. Consider hiring a local ski guide for a half-day to discover off-piste routes safely (approx. CHF 80–120 for a shared group guide).
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch on the mountain, ski until mid-afternoon then head back toward Poschiavo. Stop at Pontresina village on the way back for a short walk and to browse local sports shops or pick up Swiss souvenirs. Pontresina is a charming, less commercialized alternative to St. Moritz.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner in Poschiavo – revisit the Traditional Graubünden Fondue experience or try a different local restaurant for a celebratory end-of-skiing dinner. Toast to a great week in the Alps with local Graubünden wine (Pinot Noir from the region is excellent).

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast – pack extra snacks for the mountain
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant at Diavolezza (CHF 20–35) – try the Rösti or a hearty alpine soup
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner in Poschiavo – splurge slightly on a 3-course meal (CHF 40–55 per person) with local wine. Well-deserved after a great week!

day_by_day.notes: Saturday can be busier on the slopes as weekend visitors arrive from Italian cities (Tirano/Milan side) and Swiss cities. Head up early to beat the crowds. Ski pass again approximately CHF 60–75. Consider buying a multi-day pass if you haven't already to save money across Days 3 and 6.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning at the B&B. Enjoy a long, relaxed breakfast and soak in the mountain views from the panorama B&B. Take a gentle farewell walk through Poschiavo village – visit the historic Protestant church and the Catholic church side by side (a symbol of the valley's unique religious coexistence), and pick up last-minute local products: Bündner Nusstorte (nut tart), local honey, or dried meats as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure logistics, take one final short snowshoe or walk in the valley before packing up. Check out of the B&B and begin the journey home. The Bernina Express or regional train connects Poschiavo to Tirano (Italy) or northward to Chur and Zurich for onward flights.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home. Reflect on an incredible week of glacier skiing, scenic train journeys, cross-country trails, snowshoeing, and authentic Graubünden culture in one of Switzerland's most underrated alpine valleys.

meals.breakfast: Final full B&B breakfast – enjoy every bite!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Poschiavo village café or packed food for the train journey (CHF 10–18)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-transit meal on the way home

day_by_day.notes: Check train times carefully for the return journey – the Bernina line has specific departure times and the connection to Chur/Zurich requires planning. If flying from Zurich, allow at least 4–5 hours from Poschiavo to the airport including train transfers. The Bernina Express to Chur with onward IC to Zurich HB is the most comfortable option. Book seats in advance on busy Sunday trains.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer in advance — recommended providers include Swiss Limousine Service or a local Graubünden chauffeur company. Confirm late check-in with the B&B. Pack ski gear or arrange rental bookings for Day 2 before departure.

Head to Diavolezza Glacier Skiing — one of the crown jewels of Alpine skiing. Morning ski session on the world-renowned glacier runs with panoramic views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Arrange premium ski rental or bring personal equipment; consider booking a private ski guide for the first day to orient yourself on the glacier terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza — explore the legendary off-piste Morteratsch glacier descent (guided). The afternoon light on the glacier creates extraordinary photographic opportunities. Take the cable car back up for one final run before the lifts close. Warm up in the Diavolezza mountain restaurant with a hot chocolate or Glühwein.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Freshen up at the B&B. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Poschiavo's historic village center — enjoy Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner. Savor buckwheat pizzoccheri pasta with Valtellina Casera cheese, followed by a rich cheese fondue, paired with a curated local wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at B&B — fresh pastries, local honey, mountain cheeses, cold cuts, eggs, fresh-pressed juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Diavolezza Bergrestaurant — hearty alpine cuisine such as Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), rösti with mountain cheese, and warm apple strudel
meals.dinner: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner at a premium Poschiavo village restaurant — multi-course with local wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book a private ski guide for Diavolezza in advance — highly recommended for glacier safety and to access the best runs. Purchase a Diavolezza day ski pass (approx. CHF 70–80). Bernina Express train from Poschiavo to Pontresina takes approximately 45 minutes — check timetables at RhB (Rhaetian Railway).

day_by_day.morning: After a nourishing breakfast, board the iconic UNESCO-listed Bernina Express from Poschiavo station for the full scenic winter rail journey. Wind through dramatic Alpine landscapes — the Brusio spiral viaduct, snow-draped forests, frozen lakes, and the breathtaking Bernina Pass at 2,253m. Travel toward Tirano or up to St. Moritz for a curated morning of scenic immersion. Secure a panoramic window seat in the premium glass-roof carriage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in St. Moritz for a premium afternoon experience. Explore the world-famous resort town — visit the Engadin Museum, browse luxury boutiques on Via Serlas, or enjoy a private ice skating session on the natural frozen Lake St. Moritz. Alternatively, arrange a private horse-drawn sleigh ride across the Engadin valley floor for a quintessential Swiss luxury experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in St. Moritz before the return Bernina Express journey to Poschiavo. Dine at one of St. Moritz's celebrated restaurants — consider a reservation at a Michelin-recognized establishment for a refined multi-course Alpine-Mediterranean dinner. Return to Poschiavo by evening train; enjoy a nightcap of local Grappa or herbal schnapps at the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at B&B — seasonal fruit, bircher muesli, warm croissants, local mountain butter and jams, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch in St. Moritz — consider Kulm Hotel's restaurant or a lakeside café with panoramic Engadin views; try Engadiner Nusstorte (walnut tart) as a local specialty
meals.dinner: Premium multi-course dinner in St. Moritz at a top-tier restaurant — Alpine-inspired cuisine with wine pairing; budget CHF 150–250 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Bernina Express panoramic carriage seats well in advance through RhB website — panoramic carriages fill quickly in peak winter season. The full Poschiavo–St. Moritz journey takes approximately 1 hour. Reserve St. Moritz dinner well ahead. The sleigh ride can be arranged through local Engadin operators — approximately CHF 80–150 per person.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, travel by train to Alp Grüm station — a magical high-altitude stop perched above Poschiavo on the Bernina line. Begin a guided Cross-Country Skiing session on the Alp Grüm trails. Glide through serene, snow-covered landscapes with sweeping views of the Palü glacier and the Italian Alps. The trails are peaceful and uncrowded — a stark, beautiful contrast to the busier downhill resorts. Hire a certified cross-country ski instructor for technique refinement.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cross-country skiing through the afternoon on longer trail loops. Pack a premium thermos of hot tea or mulled wine for trail-side refreshment. As the afternoon light turns golden over the glacier, take time to simply absorb the extraordinary silence and scenery. Return to Alp Grüm station and descend back to Poschiavo by train.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the B&B — enjoy the panoramic views from the property as dusk settles over the valley. Optional: arrange an in-room or private spa treatment (massage or hot stone therapy) through a local wellness provider to soothe muscles after two days of skiing. Dinner at a cozy, upscale Poschiavo trattoria — enjoy northern Italian-influenced Graubünden cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at B&B — warm porridge with mountain honey, fresh pastries, local cheeses, cold cuts, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the B&B — artisan sandwiches, local cheese, dried meats, fruit, chocolate, and a thermos of hot soup or tea enjoyed on the trail
meals.dinner: Upscale dinner at a Poschiavo village restaurant — try Capretto (roasted kid goat), polenta taragna, and local Valposchiavo wines; finish with a Torta di Pane (bread cake) dessert

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski equipment can be rented in Poschiavo or at Alp Grüm. The train to Alp Grüm from Poschiavo takes approximately 20 minutes. Dress in breathable, moisture-wicking layers — cross-country skiing is aerobically demanding. Confirm trail conditions with local tourist office before departure.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, return to Diavolezza for a second premium ski day — this time with a focus on exploring different terrain. Take the cable car to the summit (2,978m) and enjoy the morning's freshest snow conditions. With a private guide, explore the more challenging couloirs and off-piste routes on the north face. The morning views of the Bernina massif from the summit are among the most spectacular in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the neighboring Lagalb ski area (accessible via shuttle) for afternoon skiing — a more rugged, expert-level mountain with excellent powder fields and fewer crowds. Enjoy the contrast between the two connected ski areas. End the ski day with a celebratory Aperol Spritz or Bombardino (warm egg-cream liqueur) at the mountain bar.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo. This evening, indulge in the Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner experience at its finest — book a private dining arrangement or the best table at Poschiavo's most acclaimed restaurant. Celebrate the midpoint of the trip with a premium Graubünden wine flight — Pinot Noir from Maienfeld or a Valtellina Sforzato.

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at B&B — eggs cooked to order, smoked salmon, fresh fruit salad, warm bread, and a double espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lagalb or Diavolezza mountain restaurant — try Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce) with rösti, or a premium charcuterie and cheese platter with local wine
meals.dinner: Premium private or semi-private Graubünden fondue and pizzoccheri dinner — full multi-course experience with wine flight; budget CHF 120–180 per person

day_by_day.notes: Lagalb is accessible from Diavolezza via a short shuttle — confirm connection times on-site. Both areas are covered under the same Diavolezza-Lagalb ski pass. Book the private dinner arrangement at least 48 hours in advance. Consider purchasing a 2-day ski pass for Diavolezza/Lagalb to cover Days 2 and 5 at a discounted rate.

day_by_day.morning: A gentler, restorative morning — after breakfast, embark on a guided Snowshoeing adventure in Val da Camp. Strap on premium snowshoes and trek through the enchanting side valley near Poschiavo, a pristine and tranquil wilderness area. The trail winds through ancient larch forests, frozen streams, and open alpine meadows blanketed in deep snow. A certified local mountain guide will share knowledge of the valley's ecology, history, and Romansh culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoe trek to a scenic viewpoint overlooking the valley and surrounding peaks. Enjoy a warm thermos lunch in the snow. On the return, stop at a traditional Graubünden farmstead or alpine hut for a warming drink. In the late afternoon, return to Poschiavo and spend time exploring the beautifully preserved historic village — admire the Italianate architecture, visit the local church, and browse artisan shops for Graubünden specialties and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Poschiavo — celebrate with a premium farewell dinner. Choose the finest dining option in the village or arrange a private chef experience at the B&B. Enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring the best of Graubünden and Valposchiavo cuisine — from local trout to aged mountain cheese, paired with exceptional regional wines. End the evening with a glass of aged Grappa by the fireside.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent full breakfast at B&B — fresh-baked bread, homemade jams, local honey, mountain cheeses, prosciutto crudo, soft-boiled eggs, fresh juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium packed picnic or alpine hut lunch on the Val da Camp snowshoe trail — warm soup, artisan bread, local cheese, cured meats, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner — private chef or finest village restaurant; multi-course tasting menu with Graubünden wine pairing; budget CHF 180–280 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Val da Camp snowshoe guide through the Poschiavo tourist office or a local guiding company — half-day and full-day options available. Snowshoe rental is available in Poschiavo. The village historic walk is self-guided but a local guide can be arranged for a richer cultural experience. Confirm private chef or restaurant reservation well in advance for Saturday evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — enjoy a leisurely, unhurried breakfast at the B&B, savoring the last panoramic views of the Bernina massif from the property. Pack and prepare for departure. If time allows before checkout, take a short morning walk through Poschiavo village to breathe in the crisp alpine air one last time and pick up any final local provisions — Graubünden nut tart, local wine, or artisan chocolates as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of B&B Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama. Depart via pre-arranged private luxury transfer to your onward destination — Zurich Airport (approx. 2–2.5 hours), Milan Malpensa (approx. 1.5 hours), or St. Moritz for onward connections. Alternatively, take one final scenic Bernina Express journey as a memorable send-off, watching the dramatic Alpine landscape recede as you descend toward the Italian border.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or onward travel. If flight timing allows, enjoy a final Swiss dinner at the airport or in a nearby city — consider a classic Swiss restaurant in Zurich for a Zürcher Geschnetzeltes or cheese fondue as a farewell to Switzerland.

meals.breakfast: Final full alpine breakfast at B&B — a generous spread of all local favorites; request a special farewell breakfast from the host
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route — premium airport lounge dining, or a stop at a quality restaurant along the transfer route
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or city restaurant dining depending on departure schedule — or a classic Swiss restaurant in Zurich if time permits

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer the evening before to confirm pickup time. Allow ample travel time — mountain roads in February can be affected by snow or ice. Consider purchasing travel insurance that covers alpine weather delays. Tip your B&B hosts, ski guides, and drivers generously — Swiss service professionals are exceptional and gratuities are appreciated.
